text:
maria: quick heads-up — Scout-7b int4 rollout looks promising on latency/cost but there's a small quality wobble on the GTN summarization slice. summary: - ROUGE-L down 2.3% vs int8 - median latency down 22% (p95 also improved ~10%) - per-1M-token cost estimate down ~46% (rough numbers in thread). i'm leaning canary but want product + ops guidance. gdrive: https://drive.redwood/example/scout-int4-report :eyes:
aj: thanks for the flag. can you paste the slice definition and the prompt template? curious if priming changes amplify the drop. also what's sample size?
maria: slice = "gtn_summaries_v2" (~3.5k prompts), prompt = standard summarization few-shot (3 examples). ci picks: avg length 420 tokens -> mostly long-form. full perf table in doc.
leo: 2.3% rougeL is borderline, depends on acceptance threshold. product told us 1.5% is tolerable for search/assistant, but GTN wants <1%. fallback routing idea: route 25% traffic to int8 for this slice, rest to int4. cheapest option: hybrid routing by prompt length (int4 for <=256 tokens, int8 for >256).
sam: ops note — hybrid routing is doable via existing routing flags. cheap to test: add a canary route (flag: model=scout-int4, fallback=scout-int8) + traffic=10% for 24h. if cost reduction is real we'll increase.
jess: addingbench numbers from the report:
```
int8: median latency 210ms, p95 480ms, cost per 1M tokens: $11.8
int4: median latency 165ms, p95 430ms, cost per 1M tokens: $6.4
quality delta (rougeL) int4 vs int8 = -2.3% on GTN slice
```
noted degredation more pronounced on prompts with many examples.
eli: question — was quantization static or mixed-precision? if mixed (selective fp16 kernels) quality could be improved with tiny perf penalty. we tried fp16-kv for another model and closed ~1% ROUGE gap.
ben: quick econ calc: if GTN traffic = 60M tokens/day, switching to int4 saves ~($11.8-$6.4)/1M * 60 = $318/day ≈ $9.5k/month. if quality drop costs conversion, tradeoff matters. product should estimate revenue sensitivity.
ops-bot: deploy-bot: Canary created: scout-int4-canary-4654321000 -> 10% traffic, start 4654321030, monitor windows: 1h.
jess: recommended next steps: 1) run targeted priming variants (remove one-shot examples) on 500 prompts to see sensitivity 2) start 10% canary for 24h with hybrid length-based routing 3) add a short eval to measure user-facing metrics (CTR/scoring) 4) if drop >1.5% stop canary.
maria: perfect — i'll kick off the priming ablation and prod canary. will post quick numbers in ~6h. thanks all :thumbsup:
